title: Initiative: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (runtime kernel + scheduling)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
dependencies: ENG-4822 (repro harness) needed to validate fixes deterministically
ENG-4823 (metrics) needed for alerting + canary gating
ENG-4829 (release plan) needed before Dedicated-first rollout
description:
Context
Largest Dedicated + high-throughput Hosted workloads increasingly run tensor-parallel (TP) across multiple GPUs per replica. Under sustained mixed prefill/decode load (long context + bursty concurrency), we’ve seen failure modes that look like request hangs, GPU stalls, and downstream timeouts. These inflate p99, trigger autoscaling thrash, and have escalated to Sev1 for enterprise Dedicated.

Goal (what “done” means)
1) Eliminate known runtime hangs/timeouts in TP execution under load (primary).
2) Improve detection/diagnostics so future TP stalls are caught early with actionable signals (compute vs comms vs scheduler starvation).
3) Add regression coverage (repro harness + perf canary) to prevent re-introducing TP deadlocks.
4) Provide safe mitigations (watchdogs, controlled abort/retry paths, operational runbooks) for on-call.

Success metrics (tracked weekly; baseline captured from Feb incidents + perf lab)
- TP hang rate: <= 0.02% of TP requests (no progress for > watchdog threshold, per-rank heartbeat gap) in canary; <= 0.005% in prod after rollout.
- TP-related request timeout rate: reduce by 10x vs baseline on affected Dedicated clusters (target: < 0.05% of TP requests timing out due to backend stalls).
- p99 latency: no regression > +3% at steady-state throughput for representative TP workloads (mixed prefill/decode; long-context).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD): < 2 minutes for “silent stall” signatures via dashboard + alerting.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM): < 10 minutes following runbook (drain/replace replica, load-shed, concurrency cap), without global GPU wedging.

Scope / focus areas
- Runtime scheduler: queue/backpressure interactions, prefill/decode interleaving, multi-stream coordination, fairness logic that can starve collectives.
- Kernel + comms boundary: NCCL collective ordering, stream sync points, event/graph capture constraints, “silent stall” scenarios.
- Memory/KV cache under TP: fragmentation/compaction interactions that amplify stalls or cause rank divergence.
- Observability: metrics, tracing spans, structured logs to identify compute vs comms vs scheduler.
- Reliability controls: watchdog timeouts, circuit breakers/load-shedding hooks, controlled replica drain/restart.

Out of scope
- Major architecture rewrite of TP execution.
- Model quality/evals (except as workload generator).

Milestones (6–8 weeks)
Phase 0 — Triage + deterministic repro (Week 1)
- [x] Identify top 2–3 hang signatures from incidents/support tickets and classify
- [ ] Land benchmark-lab repro harness config (ENG-4822)
- [ ] Tag incident/cluster fingerprints in tracking docs; align on “stall” definition for metrics

Phase 1 — Instrumentation + targeted fixes (Weeks 2–4)
- [ ] TP heartbeat + stall reason metrics + counters (ENG-4823)
- [ ] Scheduler guardrail: prevent collective starvation (ENG-4824)
- [ ] NCCL stream/event sync hardening (ENG-4825)
- [ ] Watchdog + safe abort/drain semantics (ENG-4826)
- [ ] KV cache compaction safety under TP (ENG-4827)

Phase 2 — Regression tests + canary rollout (Weeks 4–6)
- [ ] Add TP stress scenarios to perf-canary + thresholds/alerts (ENG-4828)
- [ ] Fault-injection / simulated stall tests in CI gating (owned by Sahana / Kira; tracked via ENG-4828 follow-ups)
- [ ] Canary in Dedicated first (1–2 accounts/clusters) → expand → Hosted

Phase 3 — Operationalization (Weeks 6–8)
- [ ] Runbook + dashboard + alerts finalized; on-call training
- [ ] Known-issues page updates, customer workaround guidance, close the loop with Support/CS
- [ ] Post-incident review items closed out / verified in prod

Canary / rollout gating (proposal; finalized in ENG-4829)
- Canary preflight:
  - TP heartbeat gaps rate stable / decreasing
  - Stall reason counters not trending up
  - No p99 regression > +3% at target throughput
  - Drain/abort events bounded and non-flapping
- Rollback triggers:
  - Any new deadlock signature that causes replica-wide wedging
  - Timeout rate doubles vs baseline for a canary account
  - Alert storms due to drain/abort loops without clear mitigation

Notes / risks
- Risk: watchdog false positives under long-context + low batch; mitigate by per-model thresholds, progressive rollout, and “warn-only” mode in early canary.
- Risk: extra stream/event sync may regress throughput; mitigate with conditionalization + microbench guardrails.
- Risk: partial fixes can shift failure mode; require observability first (ENG-4823) and perf-canary coverage (ENG-4828) before broad rollout.

Latest updates
2025-02-24 (Noah): Aligned on 3 primary signatures: (1) collective starvation with prefill-heavy queue, (2) stream/event ordering gap causing silent NCCL wait, (3) cancellation path leaving ranks mismatched. Repro work underway; instrumentation PR in progress.
2025-03-05 (Talia): Dedicated-first rollout plan drafted; gating metrics agreed with SRE. Next: land repro harness + heartbeat metrics, then begin staged canary on 1–2 Dedicated clusters.
